notes: A is the arguments of the example call `import numpy as np ; rs = np.random.RandomState(52) ; x = rs.uniform(-1., 1., (5, 5)) ; x += np.diag(np.abs(x).sum(axis=1) + 1.) ; factorMatrix1(x)`. Changed for Q32: A and B are seeded strictly diagonally dominant 5x5 matrices of their own (each diagonal entry exceeds the rest of its row by at least 1) instead of upstream's input, which is factorMatrix0's in-place output on the singular np.arange(1., 26.).reshape(5, 5): pivots of rounding residue (1e-15), 0 in Q32. B is the arguments of `import numpy as np ; rs = np.random.RandomState(53) ; x = rs.uniform(-1., 1., (5, 5)) ; x += np.diag(np.abs(x).sum(axis=1) + 1.) ; factorMatrix1(x)`.
